citations.quote: Literal-1 shall be an alphanumeric or national literal
Literal-1 shall be an alphanumeric or national literal and shall not be a zero-length literal
Identifier-1 shall be defined as an alphanumeric or national data item

cases.reason: General format identical in both editions (CANCEL {identifier-1 | literal-1 | program-prototype-name-1} ...). The slice's pointer SR-14.9.5.3-1 is the identifier-1 rule, not this one; the real twin is SR-14.9.5.3-2, which adds only the zero-length clause (a 2014+ literal form with no 2002 counterpart). The 2002 requirement is the class restriction alone, and neither pointer's evidence shows the class refusal: SR-14.9.5.3-2's witness is the zero-length case. Probes at --std 2002: numeric literal refused (COBOL1627), alphanumeric and national literals accepted. No communication-section or debugging reach (a literal).
cases.needs: its own verdict: the compiler at --std 2002 refuses CANCEL 123 (COBOL1627) and admits alphanumeric and national literals (probes cancel_lit_num.cob, cancel_lit_ok.cob); the pointer should be SR-14.9.5.3-2

citations.quote: Any USE procedures associated with any of these files are not executed
Any USE EXCEPTION procedures associated with any of these files or associated with any EC-I-O exception conditions raised for any of these files are not executed

cases.reason: The implicit-CLOSE sentence is the same; the differing words are 2002 'Any USE procedures associated with any of these files' against 2023's 'USE EXCEPTION procedures ... or associated with any EC-I-O exception conditions raised for any of these files' plus the exception-checking PERFORM WHEN sentence. The PERFORM WHEN sentence has no 2002 counterpart (no Format-3 PERFORM). The EC-I-O clause is a real textual difference: 2002 suppresses only declaratives associated with the files; a USE naming an EC-I-O exception-name is not named, so its fate on a failing implicit CLOSE in 2002 rests on 14.5.12 (uncatalogued). The pointer's witness does not compile at 2002; my probe shows the implicit close but not the error paths.
cases.needs: a 2002 witness for the implicit CLOSE (candidate: probe cancel_implicit_close.cob) and for a failing implicit CLOSE with a file USE procedure present (not shown; also needs 14.5.12 of 2002 read for EC-I-O-named declaratives)

cases.reason: The 2002 CLOSE general format has a WITH LOCK option (14.8.6.1: WITH {NO REWIND | LOCK}) that 2023 deleted (§2023:E.2). GR9 governs every CLOSE, and 2002 Table 15 gives the CLOSE WITH LOCK row symbol c ('Close file') plus e, so GR9's lock release applies to CLOSE WITH LOCK. The reader's own scope-2002 lists LOCK, but its evidence is the 2023 row's witnesses (pb235_close_unit_locks, file_sharing_seq), neither of which writes CLOSE WITH LOCK, and no 2023 witness can (the phrase is refused at --std 2023, COBOL0902). So part of the 2002 scope has no evidence at 2002 through the 2023 row: a removed form the rule's words never name. Probe close_lock_release.cob at --std 2002: a manual record lock held by A blocks B (51) and CLOSE F-A WITH LOCK releases it (B then reads 00); a SHARING WITH NO OTHER file lock blocks Y (61) and CLOSE F-X WITH LOCK releases it (Y then opens 00). So the compiler is correct, and the probe is the candidate 2002 witness. At --std 2023 the probe is refused (COBOL0902), as expected.

cases.reason: Format 1 of DISPLAY is the same in both editions. In 2002, class object covers object references (including EXCEPTION-OBJECT, SELF, SUPER and NULL), and class pointer covers data-pointer and program-pointer (2002 8.4.x: data-address-identifier and program-address-identifier also create class-pointer items). All of these are within the 2023 rule, which adds only message-tag. Communication reach: an item under a CD cannot be of class pointer in this compiler at either edition (probe disp_cd_ptr.cob is refused at both for the shared-record representation, COBOL0899), and the rule is class-based in any case, so a CD record item adds no case. Probe disp_excobj.cob: DISPLAY EXCEPTION-OBJECT is refused at 2002 with COBOL1694. Side note, not a SAME/DIFFERENT matter: DISPLAY ADDRESS OF W and DISPLAY ADDRESS OF PROGRAM are refused at both editions with the wrong diagnostic (a reserved-word error, COBOL0901/COBOL5506, rather than COBOL1694). The refusal still holds, at both editions alike.

cases.reason: The 2002 licence holds when read in full. B.3 item 1 makes the screen section and the screen format of DISPLAY processor-dependent. 3.1.5 lets an implementation leave an unclaimed processor-dependent element unimplemented, requires a compile-time warning mechanism, and does not require executable code. At --std 2002 the compiler refuses the screen section and the DISPLAY screen statement by name (COBOL1560, a42-display-screen-exception), which meets the warning mechanism, and docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 5 documents the non-support. The diagnostic cites the 2023 optional-module licence (A.4.2) rather than 2002's B.3; that is message wording, not behaviour. GR17 lives only under FORMAT 2, so nothing outside the declined facility is reached.
